summary:
TerraTrace is a web-based application that helps users explore environmental changes over time. Using NASA Earth observation data from 2000 to 2025, the application allows users to examine temperature and rainfall patterns across 11 Southeast Asian countries through interactive charts and maps. Users can also compare different countries and time periods to better understand how environmental conditions have changed.

Our project addresses the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge by helping users answer four main questions: What is changing? Where is it changing? How much has it changed? And are these changes significant? Using Python, we analyze historical data, identify trends and unusual changes, and present the results in a simple and understandable way.

This project is important because environmental changes can affect our daily lives, communities, and ecosystems. However, understanding scientific data can be overwhelming, especially for people without a science background. TerraTrace aims to make NASA environmental data more accessible and encourage people to learn about the changes happening around them.
details:
What does your project do?

TerraTrace is a web application that allows users to view temperature and rainfall data across 11 Southeast Asian countries over the past 26 years (2000–2025), using data provided by NASA.

How does it work?

Users can select their desired country and view environmental data through interactive maps and graphs. They can also compare data between countries or different time periods, identify unusual changes, and see whether there are any statistically significant trends.

What are the benefits?

Rather than having to go through large amounts of data and analyze everything manually, users can explore the results in one place. This makes it easier to identify and understand environmental trends.

What is the intended impact of your project?

We want to make environmental data more accessible, especially to students and people who have little or no experience with data analysis. Hopefully, this will encourage more people to learn about the environmental changes happening around them.

Tools/Technologies Used

We built our application using Python and Streamlit. We used Pandas and NumPy for data manipulation, SciPy for statistical analysis, Plotly for graphs, and Folium for interactive maps. Our data was collected through NASA Giovanni, using the MERRA-2 and GPCP datasets. We also used VS Code and GitHub during development.

How is your project creative?

We wanted our application to have interactive features so users could explore the data themselves. They can select different countries, compare different time periods, and investigate environmental changes through interactive maps and statistical results.

What factors did your team consider?

We wanted our application to be easy to use while keeping the data processing and calculations accurate. We also focused on making the results understandable to people without a background in environmental science or statistics.
